name: ROMANIA
lead: Romania is in Eastern Europe. Carpathian forests meet a huge river delta on the Black Sea. Bran Castle inspired the Dracula legend. Romanians speak a Latin language from Roman soldiers who settled here 2,000 years ago.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Carpathian Mountains curve through Romania like a horseshoe. Wide plains stretch south and east, watered by the Danube, Europe's second-longest river.
Where the Danube meets the Black Sea, it splits into three channels. This makes the Danube Delta, a UNESCO wetland. Over 300 bird species nest or stop here.
animals: Over 10,000 brown bears live in Romania, the most in Europe. Wolves, lynx, and chamois share the Carpathian slopes.
The Danube Delta is a pelican paradise. Great white and Dalmatian pelicans glide over the reeds in thousands. Each spring, white storks nest in Romanian villages.
culture: Craftspeople in Maramureș carve huge wooden gates that take months to finish. Embroidered blouses called ie inspired the painter Henri Matisse. Every region has its own pattern.
Folk bands play fiddles and the cobza lute. Villagers dance the hora in a circle. Romanians love polenta (mămăligă) and sour soup called ciorbă.
history: Two thousand years ago, Roman legions beat the Dacian people here. They built roads and cities. Latin mixed with the local tongue. That language is still spoken today as Romanian.

Ottomans, Habsburgs, and Russians ruled parts of the land. Romania united in 1918. Communist rule lasted until 1989, when a revolution toppled Nicolae Ceaușescu in ten days. Romania joined the EU in 2007.
wows: Roșia Montană's ancient gold landscape became a UNESCO site in 2021.
Parliament Palace in Bucharest is the world's heaviest building, at about 4 billion kg.
Bram Stoker never visited Romania, yet based Dracula's castle on Bran Castle.
Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, in 1976.
Săpânța's Merry Cemetery has colourful crosses with funny poems about the dead.
Romania has eight UNESCO painted monasteries, with frescoes on their outer walls.
Bears wander into Brașov to raid rubbish bins.

myths.fact: It is a sunny plateau ringed by mountains, with medieval walled cities like Sibiu and Sighișoara.

myths.myth: Romanians and Roma are the same people
myths.fact: No. Roma are a people spread across Europe. Romanians come from Romania. The names only sound alike.
